hooks.text: A giant shadow blocked up to twenty-two percent of a star's light.
Did an alien megastructure block twenty-two percent of a star's light?
A star lost a quarter of its light without any planet blocking it.

title: The Cosmic Mystery of Tabby's Star
description: In 2015, a star that dimmed erratically by up to 22 percent sparked wild theories about alien megastructures. Here is the true cosmic culprit.

beats.text: A giant shadow blocked up to twenty-two percent of a star's light.
beats.visual: artist's concept of KIC 8462852 showing erratic dimming

beats.text: In 2015, citizen scientists using NASA's Kepler telescope found a weirdly behaving star.
beats.visual: illustration of the Kepler space telescope in orbit, NASA, 2009

beats.text: This star, later named Tabby's Star, dimmed erratically by up to 22 percent.
beats.visual: constellation map of Cygnus highlighting Tabby's Star location

beats.text: A normal planet like Jupiter blocks only about 1 percent of a star's light.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a hot Jupiter transiting its parent star, ESO, 2018

beats.text: To explain the massive dip, some researchers speculated we were seeing an alien megastructure.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a Dyson swarm around a distant star

beats.text: But telescopes showed the light dims differently depending on its wavelength, ruling out solid structures.
beats.visual: photograph of the Allen Telescope Array antennas in California, 2015

beats.text: Instead, a massive cloud of space dust, possibly from an evaporating exomoon, is blocking the light.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a disrupted evaporating exomoon shedding dust

beats.text: This swirling dust is the true cosmic culprit casting that giant shadow.
beats.visual: artist's concept of Tabby's Star obscured by a ring of dust

better_than_last: This episode improves on ep024 by utilizing a concise 12-word statement hook and an open, seamless loop that flows directly back to the opening line.
